title: Why Openly Fake Pills Still Cut Pain

viewer_description:
At Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, Harvard Medical School researchers enrolled eighty adults with daily irritable bowel pain and gave half of them inert cellulose capsules openly marked as placebo pills. Although doctors clearly explained that zero active medication was inside, fifty-nine percent of patients taking two capsules twice daily for twenty-one days reported real symptom relief compared with thirty-five percent in the matched checkup group.

A follow-up trial of ninety-seven adults with chronic lower-back pain cut daily ache by nearly thirty percent on open placebos, while brain-wave sensors showed involuntary distress signals dropping within milliseconds.

Research: Kaptchuk et al., Harvard Medical School (2010), Carvalho et al. (2016), and Guevarra et al. (2020).
debate_question: If your doctor handed you a pill bottle openly marked fake for a stubborn back ache, would your body still calm the pain down?
